calls.reason: Scarecrow finds fluent GPT-3 output alongside errors, while OpenAI reports both successes and comprehension failures. The memorization study tests other models; this mixed evidence cannot settle the broad characterization.

BIG-bench finds large gaps from expert humans, while PaLM reports exceeding average human performance on aggregate. These differing comparisons do not settle the vague judgment about closeness to understanding.

The parsing study finds structural failures in sequence models but strong results from compositional parsers; LaMDA reports dialogue improvements. Neither settles the broad, evaluative assertion that machine language acquisition is not working.

The AMR study demonstrates mappings between text and semantic graphs in both directions. That restricted success neither establishes language acquisition comparable to children's nor supports the universal claim that no machine achieves it.
